name: E-Commerce & Retail
summary: Abandoned cart recovery, shipping updates, low-stock alerts, returns, reviews, and win-back.

automations.title: Post-Purchase Cross-Sell & Review Request Sequence
automations.summary: Seven days after a customer's first order is delivered, they automatically receive a product-specific email recommending complementary items based…
steps: Seven days after a customer's first order is delivered, they automatically receive a product-specific email recommending complementary items based on what they bought, a curated cross-sell rather than a generic "you might also like" blast.
Fourteen days after delivery, a review request goes out with a direct link to the product page, and customers who leave a review receive a thank-you discount code for their next order.
The entire post-purchase relationship is managed automatically, turning a one-time transaction into a repeat customer without the store owner building a single manual campaign.
automations.manualProcess: The manual approach means a store owner handles each case reactively, after someone has already noticed something went wrong. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.
tools: Product review app (e.g., Judge.me or Yotpo)

automations.title: Proactive Order Delay Notification & Resolution System
automations.summary: When a fulfillment delay is detected (a carrier scan gap, an out-of-stock item, or a warehouse hold) this automation identifies every affected…
steps: When a fulfillment delay is detected (a carrier scan gap, an out-of-stock item, or a warehouse hold) this automation identifies every affected order, sends each customer a proactive update before they contact support, and offers a resolution option: wait with a discount code, cancel, or switch to an in-stock alternative.

Customers who are notified proactively generate far fewer inbound support tickets and have significantly higher resolution rates than those who discovered the delay themselves, turning an operational problem into a customer loyalty moment.
automations.manualProcess: Manually, a customer service manager is stuck doing repetitive follow-ups and data entry that could otherwise run quietly in the background. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.
tools: Shipping carrier API or EasyPost (delay detection)

automations.title: Supplier Lead Time Tracker & Safety Stock Calculator
automations.summary: As purchase orders are placed and received, this automation tracks the actual lead time for each supplier and SKU, not the lead time the supplier…
steps: As purchase orders are placed and received, this automation tracks the actual lead time for each supplier and SKU, not the lead time the supplier promised, but the lead time they delivered.
Over a rolling 90-day window, it calculates average and worst-case lead times per supplier and adjusts the recommended safety stock level accordingly.

When a supplier's reliability score drops below a set threshold, the inventory manager receives an alert to either adjust reorder points or begin qualifying an alternative supplier, before a reliability issue causes a stockout that was entirely predictable in hindsight.
automations.manualProcess: Left unautomated, an inventory manager spends hours on the parts of this job that don't require judgment: copying data, sending reminders, and tracking status by hand.
tools: Inventory management platform (e.g., Cin7, Skubana, or Linnworks)
Google Sheets (lead time and safety stock model)

automations.title: Influencer & UGC Content Collection & Publishing Pipeline
automations.summary: When a customer uses the brand's hashtag, tags the brand in a post, or is identified as a micro-influencer in the product niche, this automation…
steps: When a customer uses the brand's hashtag, tags the brand in a post, or is identified as a micro-influencer in the product niche, this automation flags the content for the marketing manager to review, sends a templated DM requesting usage rights, and (once approved) adds the asset to a shared content library with tags for product, platform, and visual style.

Approved UGC is automatically scheduled into the social calendar to fill planned content slots, reducing the time spent hunting for authentic content to near zero while keeping the feed consistently fresh.
automations.manualProcess: Without a system in place, a marketing manager has to manually chase down updates, send reminders one by one, and hope nothing falls through the cracks. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.
tools: Social listening tool (e.g., Mention or a hashtag monitoring app)
Airtable or Google Sheets (UGC asset library)
Instagram and TikTok APIs (DM rights request)

automations.title: Returns & Refund Processing Automation
automations.summary: When a customer submits a return request, this automation validates the order against return policy rules (window, product eligibility, condition)…
steps: When a customer submits a return request, this automation validates the order against return policy rules (window, product eligibility, condition), generates a pre-paid shipping label, sends it to the customer immediately, and creates a refund task that routes to the operations manager for approval once the tracking shows the item has been received.
What used to be a multi-day back-and-forth email chain becomes a self-service process that handles itself in hours.
automations.manualProcess: The manual version of this puts the entire workload on an e-commerce operations manager, who has to juggle phone calls, emails, and spreadsheets just to keep things moving. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.

automations.title: Abandoned Cart Recovery Sequence
automations.summary: The moment a shopper adds items to their cart and leaves the site without checking out, this automation starts a timed recovery sequence: a reminder…
steps: The moment a shopper adds items to their cart and leaves the site without checking out, this automation starts a timed recovery sequence: a reminder email at 1 hour, a second email with a small incentive at 24 hours, and a final SMS nudge at 48 hours for shoppers who opted into texts.
Each message pulls in the actual product images and price from the abandoned cart so the shopper sees exactly what they left behind, not a generic "come back" message.

Carts recovered through this sequence convert at a meaningfully higher rate than carts left to sit untouched, turning a leaky point in the funnel into a reliable revenue source that runs without anyone monitoring it.
automations.manualProcess: Without a system in place, an ecommerce manager has to manually chase down updates, send reminders one by one, and hope nothing falls through the cracks. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.

automations.title: Back-in-Stock Alert System
automations.summary: When a customer requests notification on a sold-out product page, their email is logged against that specific SKU.
steps: When a customer requests notification on a sold-out product page, their email is logged against that specific SKU.

The instant inventory for that SKU is replenished (whether restocked in 3 days or 3 months later), every customer on the waitlist receives an email within minutes, often ahead of the general announcement, giving them first access before the item sells out again.

For high-demand items this creates a built-in early access moment that drives a fast sales spike on restock day, and it means the merchant never has to remember which customers were waiting on which product.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, this falls entirely on an ecommerce manager, who has to track every step by hand across emails, spreadsheets, and sticky notes. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.
tools: Back-in-stock app (e.g., Klaviyo forms or Swym)

automations.title: Post-Purchase Upsell Sequence
automations.summary: Rather than sending every customer the same generic follow-up email, this automation times its outreach to the actual consumption cycle of what they…
steps: Rather than sending every customer the same generic follow-up email, this automation times its outreach to the actual consumption cycle of what they bought: a customer who ordered a 30-day supply of a consumable gets a reorder reminder at day 25, while a customer who bought a durable good gets a complementary product recommendation at day 45 instead.
The recommendation logic pulls from actual purchase history rather than a static "customers also bought" list, so the offer feels relevant rather than automated.
Reorder timing that matches real usage patterns consistently outperforms a flat 30-day-for-everyone email blast, and it recovers repeat revenue the store would otherwise leave on the table.
automations.manualProcess: Without a system in place, a retention marketing manager has to manually chase down updates, send reminders one by one, and hope nothing falls through the cracks. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.
tools: Google Sheets (reorder cycle mapping by SKU)

automations.title: Automated Shipping Status Notifications
automations.summary: As a package moves through fulfillment, this automation watches the carrier tracking feed and fires an SMS at each real milestone: order shipped…
steps: As a package moves through fulfillment, this automation watches the carrier tracking feed and fires an SMS at each real milestone: order shipped, out for delivery, and delivered, instead of a single "your order shipped" email that leaves the customer checking a tracking page manually for the next week.
If a package sits without a scan update for more than 48 hours, the customer automatically receives a heads-up message rather than discovering the delay themselves.
The result is a steady drop in "where is my order" support tickets and a delivery experience that feels proactive instead of silent.
automations.manualProcess: Done by hand, this depends entirely on a customer experience manager remembering to check in, update records, and follow up, with no safety net if something slips. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.

automations.title: Post-Delivery Review Request Flow
automations.summary: Instead of asking for a review the day an order ships, this automation waits until 4 days after the estimated delivery date, giving the customer…
steps: Instead of asking for a review the day an order ships, this automation waits until 4 days after the estimated delivery date, giving the customer enough time to actually use the product before being asked to rate it.
The request includes a direct incentive for uploading a photo alongside the written review, since photo reviews convert future browsers at a noticeably higher rate than text-only reviews.
Customers who don't respond within a week get a single, friendly reminder before the request is closed out, keeping the review pipeline full without turning into spam.
automations.manualProcess: Left to a person, this means an ecommerce manager re-enters the same data more than once, double-checks it by hand, and still occasionally misses something. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.
tools: Product review app (e.g., Judge.me or Yotpo)

automations.title: Lapsed Customer Win-Back Campaign
automations.summary: When a previously active customer crosses 90 days without a purchase, this automation pulls their purchase history and builds a personalized…
steps: When a previously active customer crosses 90 days without a purchase, this automation pulls their purchase history and builds a personalized win-back email around what they bought before, along with an offer sized to their past order value rather than a blanket discount code.

Customers who still don't engage after the first email receive a second, stronger offer at day 105, and anyone who converts is automatically removed from the sequence so they don't keep receiving win-back messages.
Reactivating an existing customer this way costs a fraction of acquiring a new one, and it quietly recovers revenue from a segment most stores never revisit.
automations.manualProcess: The manual approach means an ecommerce manager handles each case reactively, after someone has already noticed something went wrong. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.

automations.title: Low Stock Auto-Reorder Alerts
automations.summary: Each SKU is assigned a reorder threshold based on its sales velocity and the supplier's typical lead time.
steps: Each SKU is assigned a reorder threshold based on its sales velocity and the supplier's typical lead time.

The moment stock on hand drops below that threshold, the inventory manager gets an immediate Slack and email alert with the recommended reorder quantity already calculated, and for established suppliers the automation can go a step further and send the purchase order directly.
This closes the gap between "someone notices stock is getting low" and "the reorder actually gets placed," which is where most stockouts on best-selling SKUs quietly happen.
automations.manualProcess: Without this system, an inventory manager manually pieces together information from different places, then has to relay it to everyone who needs it. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.
tools: Inventory management platform (e.g., Cin7 or Skubana)

automations.title: VIP Tier Auto-Upgrade System
automations.summary: As customers place orders, this automation tracks lifetime spend in real time and automatically moves them into the next loyalty tier the moment…
steps: As customers place orders, this automation tracks lifetime spend in real time and automatically moves them into the next loyalty tier the moment they cross a set threshold, no manual review, no waiting for a monthly batch update.

The newly upgraded customer immediately receives a congratulatory email laying out their new perks (free shipping, early access, a birthday reward) along with a welcome discount to use on their next order.

Customers notified the instant they hit VIP status engage with the perk far more than customers who find out about a tier change weeks later buried in a newsletter, making the loyalty program feel like a live relationship instead of a static point system.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, a loyalty program manager has to notice problems after they've already happened, then scramble to fix them manually one at a time.
tools: Loyalty platform (e.g., Smile.io or Yotpo Loyalty)

automations.title: Abandoned Cart Recovery Email & SMS Sequence
automations.summary: When a shopper on Shopify or WooCommerce adds items to their cart and leaves without completing checkout, this automation splits the response by…
steps: When a shopper on Shopify or WooCommerce adds items to their cart and leaves without completing checkout, this automation splits the response by cart value: carts under $75 enter a two-email Klaviyo sequence spaced over 36 hours, while carts above $75 get an added SMS touch through Twilio within the first two hours, since higher-value carts respond better to a faster, more direct nudge.

Zapier or Make.com watches the cart abandonment event in real time and routes each shopper into the right track automatically, pulling in the actual product image and price so the message never feels generic.

Segmenting recovery effort by cart value instead of treating every abandoned cart the same lifts recovered revenue meaningfully compared to a single one-size-fits-all sequence, without anyone on the marketing team deciding case by case who gets the extra touch.
automations.manualProcess: Left to a person, this means a growth marketing manager re-enters the same data more than once, double-checks it by hand, and still occasionally misses something. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.

automations.title: Tiered Back-in-Stock Notification System
automations.summary: When a product sells out, customers who click "notify me" on the product page are logged by SKU inside Swym or a Klaviyo back-in-stock form…
steps: When a product sells out, customers who click "notify me" on the product page are logged by SKU inside Swym or a Klaviyo back-in-stock form, building a live waitlist the merchandising team can see grow in real time.

The instant new inventory is received in Shopify or WooCommerce, Zapier or Make.com triggers a tiered release: VIP and past-purchaser segments get the restock email first, with the general waitlist following two hours later, so the highest-value customers don't lose out to a general announcement rush.

For limited-run products this staggered release turns restock day into a predictable, repeatable revenue spike instead of a chaotic first-come scramble, and it means merchandising never has to manually cross-reference who was waiting on which item.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, a merchandising manager has to notice problems after they've already happened, then scramble to fix them manually one at a time. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.

automations.title: Order Status & Shipping Update Automation
automations.summary: As an order moves from confirmed to packed to shipped to delivered, this automation pulls each fulfillment event from Shopify or WooCommerce and…
steps: As an order moves from confirmed to packed to shipped to delivered, this automation pulls each fulfillment event from Shopify or WooCommerce and AfterShip's tracking feed and fires the matching update automatically: an order confirmation the moment payment clears, a shipped notice with the tracking number as soon as the label prints, and a delivered confirmation the day the carrier marks it complete.

Zapier or Make.com routes each event to Klaviyo for email and Twilio for SMS so customers get updates in whichever channel they prefer, without a support agent ever opening the order to check its status manually.

Since "where is my order" is consistently one of the top drivers of inbound support volume for online retailers, closing that information gap removes a large share of routine tickets before they're ever opened, freeing the support team to handle questions that actually need a human.
automations.manualProcess: Manually, a customer support lead is stuck doing repetitive follow-ups and data entry that could otherwise run quietly in the background. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.

automations.title: Post-Purchase Review Request Automation
automations.summary: Five days after a Shopify or WooCommerce order shows as delivered, this automation automatically sends a review request through Klaviyo, timed so…
steps: Five days after a Shopify or WooCommerce order shows as delivered, this automation automatically sends a review request through Klaviyo, timed so the customer has actually had a chance to use the product rather than being asked to review a box they just opened.

The request links directly to the product's review form inside Judge.me or Yotpo, and customers who submit a review with a photo are automatically issued a discount code for their next order through Zapier or Make.com, since photo reviews consistently do more to convince future shoppers than text alone.
Customers who ignore the first request are queued for a single reminder rather than repeated nagging.
Running this on autopilot keeps new, authentic reviews flowing onto product pages every week without the brand manager ever having to remember which orders are due for an ask.
automations.manualProcess: Done by hand, this depends entirely on a brand manager remembering to check in, update records, and follow up, with no safety net if something slips. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.

automations.title: Multi-Touch Win-Back Campaign for Lapsed Customers
automations.summary: Once a customer's purchase history in Shopify or WooCommerce shows no order in 120 days, this automation pulls their past category and brand…
steps: Once a customer's purchase history in Shopify or WooCommerce shows no order in 120 days, this automation pulls their past category and brand preferences into Klaviyo and builds a three-email win-back arc, starting soft with a "we miss you" note and escalating to a time-limited discount by the third touch.
Customers who open but don't convert are automatically synced to a retargeting audience through Zapier or Make.com, so the offer keeps following them off-site instead of dying in an inbox.
Anyone who places an order at any point in the sequence is instantly pulled out so they don't keep receiving win-back messaging after they've already come back.
Reactivating a lapsed customer this way costs a fraction of paid acquisition and consistently recovers revenue from a segment most retailers write off entirely.
automations.manualProcess: The manual approach means a crm manager handles each case reactively, after someone has already noticed something went wrong. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.

automations.title: Low Stock Internal Alert Routing
automations.summary: Rather than relying on one person to periodically pull an inventory report, this automation watches stock levels across every SKU in Cin7 or Skubana…
steps: Rather than relying on one person to periodically pull an inventory report, this automation watches stock levels across every SKU in Cin7 or Skubana and, the moment a SKU crosses its reorder threshold, automatically routes an alert to the specific category owner responsible for that product line through Slack, cc'ing the purchasing team on anything tagged as a best-seller.

Each alert includes the current on-hand count, average weekly sales velocity, and days-of-stock remaining, pulled live from a Google Sheets model, so whoever receives it can make a reorder call in seconds rather than digging through a spreadsheet first.

Because the alert goes to the right owner immediately instead of sitting in a shared inbox, stockouts on fast-moving SKUs drop sharply, and purchasing stops finding out about a shortage only after a customer already tried to buy it.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, this falls entirely on a purchasing coordinator, who has to track every step by hand across emails, spreadsheets, and sticky notes. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.
tools: Inventory management platform (e.g., Cin7 or Skubana)

automations.title: Browsing-History Product Recommendation Email
automations.summary: Using the browsing and purchase data collected in Segment or directly inside Klaviyo, this automation builds a "you may also like" email a few days…
steps: Using the browsing and purchase data collected in Segment or directly inside Klaviyo, this automation builds a "you may also like" email a few days after a customer's most recent purchase, pulling from what they actually viewed and bought rather than a static, store-wide bestseller list.

A product recommendation engine like Rebuy or Nosto scores the catalog against that customer's behavior and feeds the top matches into the email template automatically through Zapier or Make.com, so every send is uniquely built per customer without the merchandising team hand-picking products.

Emails built this way consistently pull a meaningfully higher click-through rate than generic promotional blasts, because the products shown are ones the customer has already shown real interest in, turning a routine marketing email into a quiet, ongoing repeat-purchase driver.
automations.manualProcess: Done by hand, this depends entirely on a site merchandiser remembering to check in, update records, and follow up, with no safety net if something slips.

automations.title: VIP Customer Auto-Tagging & Perks Enrollment
automations.summary: As orders come in, this automation continuously totals each customer's lifetime spend inside Shopify or WooCommerce and, the moment a customer…
steps: As orders come in, this automation continuously totals each customer's lifetime spend inside Shopify or WooCommerce and, the moment a customer crosses a defined threshold, automatically applies a VIP tag to their profile and syncs that segment into Klaviyo through Zapier or Make.com.

The newly tagged VIP is immediately enrolled in a dedicated perks sequence: early access to new drops, a higher loyalty point multiplier inside Smile.io, and a standing free-shipping code, all without anyone on the team manually reviewing spend reports to decide who qualifies.

Because the tag updates in real time rather than during a periodic manual review, VIP customers are recognized and rewarded the same week they earn the status instead of months later, keeping the top of the customer base engaged instead of quietly churning out unnoticed.
automations.manualProcess: Left unautomated, a loyalty program manager spends hours on the parts of this job that don't require judgment: copying data, sending reminders, and tracking status by hand. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.

automations.title: Return & Exchange Automation with Instant Swap Offer
automations.summary: When a customer starts a return through the store's returns portal, this automation checks the reason given (wrong size, changed mind, defective)…
steps: When a customer starts a return through the store's returns portal, this automation checks the reason given (wrong size, changed mind, defective) and, for size or color issues, automatically offers an instant exchange instead of a refund: the replacement item ships the same day, a prepaid return label for the original goes out by email through EasyPost or ShipStation, and the order in Shopify or WooCommerce is updated to reflect the swap.
Only returns that don't qualify for an exchange fall through to a standard refund, which routes to the returns manager for approval once the original item's tracking shows it's back in the warehouse.

Offering the exchange first keeps a meaningful share of return revenue in the business instead of losing it to a refund entirely, and it turns what used to be a multi-day email thread into a same-day resolution.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, this falls entirely on a returns manager, who has to track every step by hand across emails, spreadsheets, and sticky notes. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.

automations.title: Subscription Renewal & Failed Payment Recovery
automations.summary: When a recurring subscription charge fails inside Recharge or Stripe Billing, this automation doesn't just retry the card once and give up: it…
steps: When a recurring subscription charge fails inside Recharge or Stripe Billing, this automation doesn't just retry the card once and give up: it schedules three retry attempts spaced over five days using card-updater logic, and after each failed attempt sends the customer an email through Klaviyo with a direct link to update their payment method before the subscription lapses.
If the third retry also fails, the customer gets a final SMS through Twilio warning that cancellation is imminent, giving them one last easy way to save the subscription.
Zapier or Make.com keeps the subscription status, the payment retries, and the customer messaging all in sync so nothing falls out of order.

Recovering failed payments this systematically saves a significant share of subscriptions that would otherwise churn silently over a simple expired card, protecting recurring revenue the business had already counted on.
automations.manualProcess: Done manually, a subscription manager has to remember to follow up on every case individually, often relying on memory, phone calls, and whatever notes didn't get lost. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.

automations.title: Browse Abandonment Follow-Up Email
automations.summary: When a visitor views the same product page three or more times in a session without adding it to their cart, this automation treats that as high…
steps: When a visitor views the same product page three or more times in a session without adding it to their cart, this automation treats that as high purchase intent and automatically triggers a follow-up email through Klaviyo highlighting that exact product, paired with supporting star ratings pulled from Judge.me or Yotpo and a size or color availability note.

Behavioral tracking is handled through Klaviyo's on-site tracking snippet, with Zapier or Make.com managing the trigger logic so only genuinely engaged browsers, not casual scrollers, receive the email.

Because the message targets shoppers who already showed real interest rather than a cold audience, browse abandonment emails typically convert at a noticeably higher rate than standard promotional sends, recovering purchase intent that would otherwise evaporate the moment the visitor closed the tab.
automations.manualProcess: Without this system, a digital marketing manager manually pieces together information from different places, then has to relay it to everyone who needs it. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.

automations.title: Fraud & Risk Order Flagging System
automations.summary: As each order comes through checkout, this automation runs it against a risk model inside Signifyd or NoFraud, checking for mismatched billing and…
steps: As each order comes through checkout, this automation runs it against a risk model inside Signifyd or NoFraud, checking for mismatched billing and shipping addresses, an order value far above the customer's typical spend, or an account created minutes before the purchase.

Orders that score above the risk threshold are automatically held from fulfillment in Shopify or WooCommerce and routed to the risk manager through Slack with the specific red flags attached, rather than shipping on autopilot and hoping for the best.
Zapier or Make.com handles the hold-and-notify logic so nothing risky slips through during a busy sales period.

Catching high-risk orders before they ship prevents a meaningful share of chargebacks and fraudulent-order losses that would otherwise only surface weeks later as a dispute, protecting margin on exactly the orders that looked fine at a glance.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, this falls entirely on a risk & fraud manager, who has to track every step by hand across emails, spreadsheets, and sticky notes. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.

automations.title: Checkout Cross-Sell Automation
automations.summary: Based on the specific items already sitting in a shopper's cart, this automation surfaces complementary product suggestions directly on the checkout…
steps: Based on the specific items already sitting in a shopper's cart, this automation surfaces complementary product suggestions directly on the checkout page through Rebuy or a native Shopify checkout extension, a phone case shown next to a new phone, a matching accessory next to a dress, rather than a generic "frequently bought together" module unrelated to the actual cart contents.

The recommendation logic runs off real co-purchase data pulled from order history, refreshed weekly through Zapier or Make.com, so the suggestions stay accurate as the catalog and buying patterns shift.

Because the offer appears at the exact moment a customer is already committed to buying, checkout cross-sells convert at a far higher rate than post-purchase upsell emails, quietly lifting average order value on every transaction without the merchandising team touching a single product page.
automations.manualProcess: Left to a person, this means an ecommerce manager re-enters the same data more than once, double-checks it by hand, and still occasionally misses something. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.

automations.title: Support Ticket Auto-Routing System
automations.summary: As inquiries land in Gorgias or Zendesk, this automation reads the subject line and message content and automatically categorizes each ticket…
steps: As inquiries land in Gorgias or Zendesk, this automation reads the subject line and message content and automatically categorizes each ticket, shipping issue, return request, product question, billing problem, then routes it to the team or agent best equipped to handle it, tagging order-related tickets with the actual order data pulled from Shopify or WooCommerce so the agent never has to ask the customer to repeat themselves.
Urgent categories like "damaged item" or "never arrived" are automatically flagged as priority and routed to the front of the queue through Zapier or Make.com.

Instead of every ticket sitting in one general inbox waiting to be manually triaged, tickets reach the right agent within minutes of arriving, cutting average first-response time significantly and keeping the support team focused on solving problems instead of sorting them.
automations.manualProcess: The manual version of this puts the entire workload on a customer support manager, who has to juggle phone calls, emails, and spreadsheets just to keep things moving.

automations.title: Affiliate & Influencer Commission Tracking
automations.summary: Every sale that comes through an affiliate or influencer's unique link is automatically tracked back to its source using Refersion or ReferralCandy…
steps: Every sale that comes through an affiliate or influencer's unique link is automatically tracked back to its source using Refersion or ReferralCandy, attributing the order, commission rate, and payout amount without anyone cross-referencing UTM parameters by hand.

At the end of each pay period, Zapier or Make.com compiles a commission report per affiliate into Google Sheets, and approved payouts are pushed automatically through PayPal or Stripe rather than being calculated and issued manually one at a time.
Affiliates get a self-serve dashboard showing their real-time sales and pending commission, which keeps them motivated to keep posting without needing a status update from the marketing team.
Automating tracking and payout removes what used to be hours of manual reconciliation every month and keeps the affiliate program accurate enough that partners actually trust the numbers.
automations.manualProcess: Without this system, an affiliate marketing manager manually pieces together information from different places, then has to relay it to everyone who needs it.

automations.title: Loyalty Points Expiration Reminder
automations.summary: As loyalty points inside Smile.io or LoyaltyLion approach their expiration date, this automation automatically identifies every customer with unused…
steps: As loyalty points inside Smile.io or LoyaltyLion approach their expiration date, this automation automatically identifies every customer with unused points expiring in the next 14 days and sends a reminder email through Klaviyo showing exactly how many points they have and what those points are worth toward their next order.
Customers with a meaningful balance, enough to cover a real discount, not just a few cents, get a slightly more urgent second reminder at the 3-day mark through Zapier or Make.com.

Because the message creates genuine urgency around something the customer already owns rather than asking them to act on a generic sale, expiration reminders convert to a purchase at a notably higher rate than standard promotional email, recovering revenue from points that would otherwise quietly expire unused and unnoticed.
automations.manualProcess: Manually, a customer loyalty coordinator is stuck doing repetitive follow-ups and data entry that could otherwise run quietly in the background. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.

automations.title: First-Time Buyer Welcome Series
automations.summary: The moment a customer completes their very first order in Shopify or WooCommerce, this automation enrolls them in a dedicated welcome series through…
steps: The moment a customer completes their very first order in Shopify or WooCommerce, this automation enrolls them in a dedicated welcome series through Klaviyo that's entirely separate from the store's general newsletter: the brand's origin story on day one, product care and usage tips on day three, tailored to whatever category they actually bought, and an invitation to the referral program on day seven with a friend discount code.
Zapier or Make.com confirms the order is genuinely a first purchase before enrollment, so returning customers never get a "welcome" email they've already seen.

New customers who go through a structured welcome series place a second order sooner and more often than those simply dropped into the general marketing list, making this one of the highest-leverage sequences a store can automate.
automations.manualProcess: Left to a person, this means a customer marketing manager re-enters the same data more than once, double-checks it by hand, and still occasionally misses something. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.

automations.title: Wishlist Price-Drop Alert
automations.summary: When a customer saves an item to their wishlist using Swym or a native wishlist app, this automation keeps watching that product's price in the…
steps: When a customer saves an item to their wishlist using Swym or a native wishlist app, this automation keeps watching that product's price in the background, and the instant it drops, whether from a scheduled sale or a manual markdown, the customer automatically receives a notification through Klaviyo showing the old price crossed out next to the new one.
Zapier or Make.com checks price changes against the full wishlist database daily so no drop goes unnoticed, even on obscure, low-traffic SKUs the pricing team might not think to promote directly.

Because the alert reaches a customer who already decided they wanted the item and was only waiting on price, wishlist price-drop emails convert at a rate few other campaigns can match, turning routine markdowns into an active sales channel instead of a passive price change nobody notices.
automations.manualProcess: Left to a person, this means a pricing manager re-enters the same data more than once, double-checks it by hand, and still occasionally misses something.

automations.title: Marketplace Inventory Sync Across Sales Channels
automations.summary: As orders come in from the website, Amazon, and Etsy simultaneously, this automation keeps stock counts synced across every channel in real time…
steps: As orders come in from the website, Amazon, and Etsy simultaneously, this automation keeps stock counts synced across every channel in real time through a centralized platform like Extensiv or ChannelAdvisor, deducting inventory the instant a sale happens anywhere so the same unit can never be sold twice.

Zapier or Make.com handles the connection between the sync platform and each individual marketplace API, and if a sync fails or a channel drifts out of range of actual stock, the operations manager gets an immediate Slack alert rather than finding out from an angry customer email.

Before this kind of sync was in place, overselling on a fast-moving SKU across multiple channels was a routine, expensive problem; keeping every channel mirrored in real time eliminates it almost entirely and protects the business from the cancellations and account strikes that oversold marketplace orders cause.
automations.manualProcess: Handled by hand, an operations manager spends time each day re-checking the same information across disconnected tools instead of doing higher-value work. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.

automations.title: Post-Return Win-Back Offer
automations.summary: Rather than letting a returned order be the last interaction a customer has with the brand, this automation triggers the moment a return is…
steps: Rather than letting a returned order be the last interaction a customer has with the brand, this automation triggers the moment a return is completed in Shopify or WooCommerce and automatically sends a thoughtful follow-up through Klaviyo a few days later: an alternative product suggestion based on why the item was returned (a different size, a different style, a different scent) paired with a modest incentive to try again.

Returns flagged as quality issues are routed to a slightly more generous offer than returns flagged as "changed mind," since the brand is asking the customer to trust it again after a real product problem.
Zapier or Make.com manages the return-reason logic so the right offer reaches the right customer automatically.

Customers who receive this follow-up return to purchase again at a meaningfully higher rate than those simply refunded and left alone, turning a moment of disappointment into a second chance at the relationship.
automations.manualProcess: Left unautomated, a customer retention manager spends hours on the parts of this job that don't require judgment: copying data, sending reminders, and tracking status by hand. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.

automations.title: Pre-Order Launch Notification
automations.summary: Customers who place a pre-order in Shopify or WooCommerce are automatically added to a dedicated launch-day segment inside Klaviyo, separate from…
steps: Customers who place a pre-order in Shopify or WooCommerce are automatically added to a dedicated launch-day segment inside Klaviyo, separate from the general customer list, so they can be messaged specifically about that product without cluttering the inbox of anyone who hasn't ordered it.

The moment inventory is received and the product flips to "in stock" or the fulfillment run begins shipping, Zapier or Make.com fires an immediate notification through email and, for customers who opted in, a Twilio SMS confirming their order is on its way, without anyone on the team having to remember which pre-orders are pending on which exact day.

Customers who pre-ordered and then hear nothing until a surprise shipping confirmation are far more likely to file a "where is my order" ticket than those kept informed in real time, so this alone measurably reduces launch-week support volume.
automations.manualProcess: The manual version of this puts the entire workload on a product launch manager, who has to juggle phone calls, emails, and spreadsheets just to keep things moving. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.

automations.title: Gift Purchase Recipient Follow-Up
automations.summary: When a customer marks an order as a gift at checkout in Shopify or WooCommerce, this automation waits until a few days after the estimated delivery…
steps: When a customer marks an order as a gift at checkout in Shopify or WooCommerce, this automation waits until a few days after the estimated delivery date and then sends the purchaser, not the recipient, a friendly follow-up through Klaviyo asking whether the gift landed well, paired with a discount code for their own next purchase as a thank-you for shopping the brand for someone else.
Zapier or Make.com filters specifically for orders tagged as gifts so regular customers never receive a message that wouldn't make sense for their own purchase.

Because the follow-up targets a moment of genuine emotional payoff, giving a gift that was well received, rather than a routine transactional touchpoint, it converts the purchaser into a repeat customer for themselves at a noticeably higher rate than a standard post-purchase email, extending one gift purchase into an ongoing relationship.
automations.manualProcess: The manual version of this puts the entire workload on a gifting & promotions manager, who has to juggle phone calls, emails, and spreadsheets just to keep things moving. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.
tools: Discount code generator (native platform or Klaviyo)

automations.title: Bundle Component Inventory Alert
automations.summary: When a bundled product sells in Shopify or WooCommerce, this automation automatically deducts each individual component from its own inventory count…
steps: When a bundled product sells in Shopify or WooCommerce, this automation automatically deducts each individual component from its own inventory count inside Cin7 or Skubana rather than only decrementing the bundle SKU itself, so the true stock picture for every component stays accurate even as it's sold both individually and inside bundles.

If any component's remaining stock would fall short of what's needed to fulfill an already-placed bundle order, the supply chain manager gets an immediate Slack alert through Zapier or Make.com before the order ships incomplete.

This catches the specific failure mode where a bundle looks purchasable on the storefront because the bundle SKU shows in stock, even though one component quietly ran out weeks earlier, preventing the kind of partial-shipment customer complaint that's expensive to fix after the fact and easy to prevent before it happens.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, a supply chain manager has to notice problems after they've already happened, then scramble to fix them manually one at a time.
tools: Inventory management platform (e.g., Cin7 or Skubana)

automations.title: Lifetime Value Segmentation Campaign
automations.summary: Using order history pulled from Shopify or WooCommerce, this automation continuously recalculates each customer's lifetime spend and automatically…
steps: Using order history pulled from Shopify or WooCommerce, this automation continuously recalculates each customer's lifetime spend and automatically sorts them into tiers, entry-level, core, and top-spender, inside Klaviyo, updating segment membership in real time as new orders come in rather than during an occasional manual export.

Each tier automatically receives different campaign treatment: entry-level customers get frequency-focused offers designed to earn a second order, while top-spender customers get early access and higher-value perks rather than the same blanket 10%-off code everyone else sees.
Zapier or Make.com keeps the tier logic synced between the store and the email platform so no customer is ever messaged based on stale data.

Treating customers differently based on actual value, instead of sending one campaign to the entire list, measurably lifts revenue per email sent and keeps top customers from feeling like just another name on the list.
automations.manualProcess: Manually, a customer data manager is stuck doing repetitive follow-ups and data entry that could otherwise run quietly in the background.
tools: Google Sheets or a CDP (e.g., Segment)

automations.title: Escalating Review Reminder for Non-Responders
automations.summary: When a customer doesn't respond to the initial post-delivery review request sent through Klaviyo, this automation doesn't just resend the same…
steps: When a customer doesn't respond to the initial post-delivery review request sent through Klaviyo, this automation doesn't just resend the same email; seven days later it sends a single follow-up reminder with a slightly different subject line and a small added incentive, a modest discount or loyalty points, for customers who complete a review this time.
Zapier or Make.com tracks whether the review was actually submitted in Judge.me or Yotpo before triggering the reminder, so customers who already left a review never get a redundant nag.
After the second reminder goes unanswered, the customer is removed from the sequence entirely rather than being pestered further.

This single, well-timed follow-up recovers a meaningful share of reviews that the first ask alone would have missed, keeping product pages stocked with fresh social proof without crossing into spam territory.
automations.manualProcess: Without a system in place, a reviews & reputation manager has to manually chase down updates, send reminders one by one, and hope nothing falls through the cracks. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.

automations.title: International Customs Documentation Automation
automations.summary: The moment an order ships to an international address, this automation automatically generates the required customs paperwork, commercial invoice…
steps: The moment an order ships to an international address, this automation automatically generates the required customs paperwork, commercial invoice, HS codes, declared value, using Zonos or Avalara's cross-border compliance engine, pulling the product details directly from Shopify or WooCommerce so nothing has to be typed in by hand.

The completed documentation is attached directly to the shipping label generated through EasyPost or ShipStation before it ever reaches the warehouse floor, so the fulfillment team never has to pause an international order to track down paperwork.
Zapier or Make.com flags any order with missing or ambiguous product data before it ships, rather than letting it get held at customs.

Manual customs paperwork is one of the most error-prone parts of international fulfillment; automating it removes the delays and returned shipments that come from a mistyped HS code or a missing invoice.
automations.manualProcess: Left to a person, this means a logistics manager re-enters the same data more than once, double-checks it by hand, and still occasionally misses something. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.

automations.title: Chargeback & Dispute Alert System
automations.summary: The moment a customer's bank initiates a chargeback through Stripe or PayPal, this automation immediately alerts the finance manager through Slack…
steps: The moment a customer's bank initiates a chargeback through Stripe or PayPal, this automation immediately alerts the finance manager through Slack with the disputed order attached, including the original order details, tracking confirmation, and the full email and support ticket history with that customer pulled from Gorgias, everything needed to build a dispute response without hunting across four different systems under a deadline.

Zapier or Make.com assembles the evidence packet automatically and, for chargeback types with a clear paper trail (delivered and tracked, for example), can submit the initial response through Signifyd or the payment processor's dispute API without waiting on a person to start the process.

Responding to a chargeback within hours instead of days meaningfully improves the win rate on disputes, and having the evidence compiled automatically means a real order dispute is never missed simply because the alert got buried in a shared inbox.
automations.manualProcess: The manual version of this puts the entire workload on a finance manager, who has to juggle phone calls, emails, and spreadsheets just to keep things moving. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.

automations.title: Seasonal Purchase History Re-Engagement
automations.summary: Using prior-year order data stored in Shopify or WooCommerce, this automation identifies every customer who bought a seasonal item, holiday decor…
steps: Using prior-year order data stored in Shopify or WooCommerce, this automation identifies every customer who bought a seasonal item, holiday decor, swimwear, back-to-school supplies, the previous year and automatically re-engages them through Klaviyo as that same season approaches again, timed to roughly two weeks before their prior purchase date so the offer lands right as they're starting to think about it.

The campaign references the specific item or category they bought before rather than a generic seasonal blast, since "the swim cover-up you loved last June is back" performs meaningfully better than "summer sale starts now."
Zapier or Make.com rebuilds this segment automatically each year rather than requiring the lifecycle team to pull the list manually every season.
Timing outreach to a customer's actual past buying rhythm consistently outperforms a calendar-based campaign sent to the entire list at once.
automations.manualProcess: Left to a person, this means a lifecycle marketing manager re-enters the same data more than once, double-checks it by hand, and still occasionally misses something.

automations.title: Out-of-Stock Substitute Suggestion
automations.summary: When a customer tries to purchase an item that's sold out, instead of hitting a dead "out of stock" page, this automation automatically surfaces a…
steps: When a customer tries to purchase an item that's sold out, instead of hitting a dead "out of stock" page, this automation automatically surfaces a similar in-stock alternative pulled from the same category using Rebuy or Nosto's product-matching logic, factoring in price range, style, and past purchase behavior when the shopper has an account.

The substitute appears directly on the product page and is also included if the customer had already requested a back-in-stock notification, giving them an immediate option instead of a wait with no clear end date.
Zapier or Make.com keeps the substitute mapping updated as inventory shifts, so a suggested alternative is never itself sold out.

Offering a real alternative in the moment recovers a meaningful share of sales that would otherwise be lost entirely to a dead end, turning what used to be an abandoned session into a completed order.
automations.manualProcess: Left unautomated, a conversion rate manager spends hours on the parts of this job that don't require judgment: copying data, sending reminders, and tracking status by hand. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.

automations.title: VIP Early Access to New Product Launches
automations.summary: Customers already tagged as VIP based on lifetime spend or loyalty tier inside Smile.io are automatically added to a dedicated early-access segment…
steps: Customers already tagged as VIP based on lifetime spend or loyalty tier inside Smile.io are automatically added to a dedicated early-access segment in Klaviyo, and whenever a new product line is scheduled to launch, this automation sends that segment a private preview and early purchase link 24 to 48 hours before the line goes live to the general public.
Zapier or Make.com handles the timing so the early-access email fires from a single launch date entered once, rather than someone manually building a VIP-only send for every new release.

Because VIP customers get first pick before inventory is public, popular sizes and colors in a new line are far less likely to sell out on the VIP shoppers specifically, a subtle but real driver of loyalty.
Rewarding VIP status with genuine first access, not just a discount, keeps top customers feeling recognized rather than treated the same as everyone else.
automations.manualProcess: Done by hand, this depends entirely on a vip experience manager remembering to check in, update records, and follow up, with no safety net if something slips. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.

automations.title: Birthday Month Personalized Discount Automation
automations.summary: Customers automatically receive a personalized discount code during their birthday month, pulled directly from their stored profile data, without…
steps: Customers automatically receive a personalized discount code during their birthday month, pulled directly from their stored profile data, without the customer marketing manager building and sending a manual birthday list every single month.

The offer is timed to arrive at the start of the birthday month, giving customers plenty of time to actually use it, and birthday campaigns consistently convert at a noticeably higher rate than a generic promotional email since the offer feels personal rather than mass-blasted.
automations.manualProcess: Done manually, a customer marketing manager has to remember to follow up on every case individually, often relying on memory, phone calls, and whatever notes didn't get lost.

steps: After a purchase, customers are automatically prompted to register their product's warranty, building a clean database that makes future service or replacement claims far faster to process instead of a customer support manager trying to verify a purchase date from an old email receipt months or years later.

Registered customers get a smoother, faster experience the moment something actually goes wrong with a product, and the warranty database itself becomes a valuable source of customer contact data for future product announcements and recall notices.
automations.manualProcess: Left unautomated, a customer support manager spends hours on the parts of this job that don't require judgment: copying data, sending reminders, and tracking status by hand. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.

steps: When a free product is sent to an influencer, the automation automatically sends a follow-up request for the agreed content and tag within the negotiated timeframe, instead of the affiliate marketing manager manually tracking dozens of individual gifting agreements in a spreadsheet and remembering to follow up on each one.

Influencers who go quiet past the agreed window get a second, friendlier reminder automatically, and the brand actually collects on the content it paid to send out instead of a meaningful share of gifted product simply never resulting in a post.
automations.manualProcess: Left to a person, this means an affiliate marketing manager re-enters the same data more than once, double-checks it by hand, and still occasionally misses something. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.

automations.summary: When customers repeatedly search for a term that returns no results, the automation automatically flags it internally, surfacing either a real…
steps: When customers repeatedly search for a term that returns no results, the automation automatically flags it internally, surfacing either a real product gap worth sourcing or a fixable search and SEO issue, a common misspelling or a product that exists under different terminology than customers actually search for.

The site merchandiser gets a ranked list of the most frequent no-result searches instead of that valuable signal disappearing silently into site analytics nobody has time to dig through, and closing even a handful of these gaps routinely recovers sales that were quietly walking away empty-handed.
automations.manualProcess: The manual approach means a site merchandiser handles each case reactively, after someone has already noticed something went wrong. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.
tools: Google Sheets or Airtable (search gap tracker)

automations.title: Free-Shipping Threshold Cart Nudge
automations.summary: Customers whose cart total sits just below the free-shipping threshold automatically see a real-time nudge suggesting a specific, relevant item to…
steps: Customers whose cart total sits just below the free-shipping threshold automatically see a real-time nudge suggesting a specific, relevant item to add and unlock free shipping, instead of the shopper simply checking out short of the threshold and paying for shipping, or worse, abandoning the cart entirely over a shipping fee.

The conversion rate manager can see exactly how much incremental revenue this single nudge generates in add-on items, and average order value climbs measurably once customers are shown a clear, easy way to get something they were probably going to buy eventually for free.

steps: Based on the typical reorder timing for a consumable product, customers automatically receive a "running low, time to reorder" reminder timed to when they're actually likely running out, rather than a generic reminder sent on an arbitrary fixed schedule that either arrives too early or too late.

The subscription manager can see reorder rates climb once reminders are timed to real consumption patterns instead of a flat calendar interval, and customers appreciate a reminder that shows up exactly when they were about to need it rather than nagging them before they've used half the product.

Every new order refines the profile a little further, so campaigns can target "customers who buy premium skincare and spend above average" with genuine precision instead of broad, guessed-at segments, and marketing spend goes toward messages that are actually relevant to the person receiving them.

automations.title: Damaged-in-Transit Claim Automation
automations.summary: A customer reporting a damaged item automatically receives the claims form along with clear next steps, and the shipment is simultaneously flagged…
steps: A customer reporting a damaged item automatically receives the claims form along with clear next steps, and the shipment is simultaneously flagged internally to start a carrier damage claim, instead of the returns manager handling the customer conversation and the carrier claim as two entirely separate manual processes that often fall out of sync.

Customers get a resolution moving immediately instead of waiting on a support agent to notice and manually kick off the carrier claim days later, and the business actually recovers more of what it's owed from carriers since claims get filed within their required window instead of occasionally missing it.

automations.title: Inactive Subscriber Re-Permission Sweep

steps: Email subscribers who haven't engaged in a long stretch automatically receive a re-permission campaign asking if they'd like to stay subscribed before being removed from the active list, protecting the sender's deliverability reputation instead of the lifecycle marketing manager letting a growing pool of disengaged addresses quietly drag down open rates and trigger spam filters.

Subscribers who confirm they still want the emails get reactivated as engaged contacts, while genuinely inactive addresses get cleanly removed, and the active list that's left behind performs measurably better across every campaign sent to it.
automations.manualProcess: Without this system, a lifecycle marketing manager manually pieces together information from different places, then has to relay it to everyone who needs it.

steps: Orders placed for local pickup automatically notify the customer the moment the order is packed and waiting at the counter, instead of the customer guessing when to come by and either showing up too early or letting the order sit unclaimed for days.

The ecommerce manager sees pickup turnaround times improve once customers know exactly when to come, and staff stop fielding "is my order ready yet" calls that used to interrupt other work throughout the day for orders that weren't even close to done.
automations.manualProcess: The manual version of this puts the entire workload on an ecommerce manager, who has to juggle phone calls, emails, and spreadsheets just to keep things moving. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.
